name: Oklahoma veterans: state service officers for claims help
organization: Oklahoma Department of Veterans Affairs service officers
description: Free help from Oklahoma Department of Veterans Affairs service officers with VA claims, appeals, pension and survivor benefits, plus state benefits. Oklahoma has no county veterans offices; four regional teams (Northwest, Northeast, Southeast and Southwest) divide the state’s 77 counties.
next_step: Choose your county for the team that serves it, or call the department’s central office at 405-523-4000 (toll-free 855-701-6382) to be matched with a service officer and to ask where and when officers meet veterans near you.
constraints: The team pages print no office hours, so call to schedule before you travel.
Some counties are listed under two teams; ask which officer is assigned to you.

name: Oklahoma Aging and Disability Info-Line
organization: Oklahoma Human Services, Community Living, Aging and Protective Services
description: Oklahoma’s free statewide aging line. It connects older Oklahomans and their caregivers to information and help from the area agency on aging nearest to the caller, with meals, transportation, in-home help and more. Military service is not required.
next_step: Call 800-211-2116, or choose a county above for its area agency on aging.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.
The line is routed to a local agency, so give your county or town.

name: Medicare counseling (Medicare Assistance Program) for Oklahoma
organization: Oklahoma Insurance Department, Medicare Assistance Program
description: Free, confidential help with Medicare choices, enrollment and costs. The Oklahoma Insurance Department’s Medicare Assistance Program runs the State Health Insurance Counseling Program (SHIP) and the Senior Medicare Patrol.
next_step: Call 800-763-2828 (direct line 405-521-6628). For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: Have your Medicare card and your drug list ready for a plan question.

source_evidence.title: Oklahoma Insurance Department: Medicare Assistance Program
source_evidence.scope: Program description, SHIP and Senior Medicare Patrol, in-state toll-free 800-763-2828 and direct line 405-521-6628; search excerpt.

name: Oklahoma Long-Term Care Ombudsman and adult abuse reporting
organization: Oklahoma Office of the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman
description: Advocacy for residents of nursing homes, assisted living and similar adult care homes, delivered through the area agencies on aging’s ombudsman supervisors and volunteers.
next_step: Call 800-211-2116 and give the county and facility name, or reach the State Ombudsman at 405-521-6734. To report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation of a vulnerable adult, call the Abuse and Neglect Hotline at 800-522-3511, 24 hours a day, or report online at OKHotline.org. For immediate danger, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing or enforcement agency; complaints to the licensing agency go to the Oklahoma State Department of Health.

name: Free legal help for Oklahoma veterans and older adults
organization: Legal Aid Services of Oklahoma; OK-SPLASH; Oklahoma Lawyers for America’s Heroes
description: Legal Aid Services of Oklahoma (LASO) gives free civil legal help to low-income Oklahomans and takes applications by phone. OK-SPLASH, run with Oklahoma Human Services, gives free legal advice to Oklahomans age 60 and older. The Oklahoma Bar Association’s Lawyers for America’s Heroes program offers free legal advice and assistance to veterans.
next_step: Call LASO at 888-534-5243 (Monday through Thursday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.), or OK-SPLASH at 855-488-6814 if you are 60 or older. Veterans can also ask about the Lawyers for America’s Heroes program at okbarheroes.org.
constraints: LASO handles civil, non-criminal cases and screens by income and household size.
Most free legal programs screen by income, case type and location; ask which you qualify for.

name: VA health care systems serving Oklahoma
description: Oklahoma veterans are served mainly by the Oklahoma City VA Health Care System (medical center at 921 N.E. 13th Street, Oklahoma City, 405-456-1000, toll-free 866-835-5273) and the Eastern Oklahoma VA Health Care System (Jack C. Montgomery VA Medical Center at 1011 Honor Heights Drive, Muskogee, 888-397-8387).
next_step: Use VA’s facility locator with your ZIP code to find the closest clinic and its medical center. Not enrolled yet? Ask a state service officer for help applying.
constraints: Which system serves a county depends on where you live; VA’s locator shows the right clinic.
